title: Work-head positions during a leftward scan
statement: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a state set, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with states in $S$. Suppose that for every input and work-tape symbols, in state $s$ the machine moves left and stays in $s$ when it scans an input symbol, and moves right and enters the optional destination state $d$ when it scans a blank; these transitions write nothing on the work tapes, move no work-tape heads, and emit no output. For every $j \in \mathbb{N}$ and configuration $c$ on $x$ in state $s$ with input-head position exactly $j$, if $j \le |x|$, then for every $u \le j+1$ the work-tape head positions after $u$ steps from $c$ equal those in $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $k$ of work tapes
A machine over the Boolean alphabet with states in $S$
For every input and work symbols, the transition from $s$ is leftward to $s$ on a symbol and rightward to $d$ on a blank
$j$ is at most the length of $x$
